name: Linn
description:
**Key Demographics: ** Humans
**Capital City: ** Straumfjord

#### Entanglements

**To the South East (via Thin Coast):**: Valewood – The portage across the Thin Coast brings iron and amber; the trees watch the passage. The portage is a treaty, not a road.
**To the West (via the Aberderrin Sea):**: Mistlands – The fog-bells and sea-roads are respected; a Linn raider knows which bell means “welcome” and which means “trap.” The fog is a better ally than any flag.
**To the Far South:**: The Dolmis Sea – Zakov and Aelinnel are destinations for trade and plunder; the tides are a better map than any chart. The sea-queen's words carry across the water.
**To the West:**: The Aberderrin Sea – The ice and the deep currents define the edge of the world; the dead lie beneath the keel. The northern horizon is a silence that listens.

### Region Diagnostic

**Current Hook (one sentence)**

[][l]{%
minipage{}

The sea keeps better counsel than any scribe, and the frost remembers every oath sworn upon its winds — but the Temple of Light arrives with ink and fire to rewrite what the ice has carved.

minipage}

**Core Conflict (one sentence)**

[][l]{%
minipage{}

Players are caught between the Jarls' raiding economy, the Sea-Queen's coastal law, and the Temple of Light's crusade of re-education and assimilation — each demanding oaths that contradict the others.

minipage}

**The One Thing Only This Region Does**

[][l]{%
minipage{}

**Frost-Bound Memory:** Oaths are carved in ice that never fully melts; breaking a storm-oath inflicts mechanical penalties (Fatigue/Harm) and gives the GM free Story Beats representing the sea's attention.

minipage}

**Interactive Mechanics (player-facing)**

**{1}**: **tv\'{**h\"{o}gg (Double-Cut Fate):} Once per session, cut one thread of fate to redirect another — succeed but mark Frost Mark, or reroll sea/oath rolls but your name is added to hidden ice.
**{2}**: **Storm-Oaths:** Swear by touching salt water; keeping grants $+1$ die on sea rolls, breaking inflicts 1 Fatigue (or 1 Harm if sworn during storm).
**{3}**: **Frost Mark (Weight Timer ):** Every favor/gift from Linn creates a 4-segment timer; when full, community demands service (raid, story, labor). Refusal = $-1$ die on social rolls.
**{4}**: **Season's Turn:** GM spends 3 SB to change season; Spring (foraging/healing $+1$), Summer (combat/sailing $+1$), Autumn (social/legal $+1$), Winter (survival Desperate, Frost Mark easier to clear).

**Campaign Timers (GM-facing)**

- **Temple Pressure [6]** – *Advances when:* players accept Temple aid, ignore shrine offerings, or fail faith tests. *At full:* Bishop demands public oath of loyalty; shrine-devout suffer $-1$ Position in settlements.
- **Thing Schism [6]** – *Advances when:* jarls convert, feuds go unresolved, or oath-rings are broken. *At full:* The Thing splits; half the clans follow Temple law, half follow frost-law. Civil conflict begins.
- **Winter Debts [8]** – *Advances when:* players accept Frost Marks, take shelter, or break small taboos. *At full:* The Thing convenes; party must defend oaths or be forced into a quest to pay debts.

**Faction Triad**

Faction in the Realm:
| |p{0.25}|p{0.25}|p{0.2}|}

**Faction** | **Goal** | **Method** | **Why players care** |
| — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — |
| **High Jarls** | Unite scattered strands under one raiding oath | Successful raids, wise judgments at Thing-Holm, frost-mark enforcement | Control harbor access, levy ships, offer raid-truces and oar-shares |
| **Sea-Queen** | Maintain coastal law without drawing blade | Envoy network, seal-bags, oath-sticks branded with queen's mark | Grants harbor-marks, escort writs, audience that bends sea-law |
| **Temple of Light Crusade** | Convert Linn to Lens of White Flame (re-education | assimilation) | Grain fleets, synod courts, bell-tower consecrations, schoolmasters | Cheap grain, legal alternatives to blood-feuds, protection from “pagan” hazards |

**The Price**

[][l]{%
minipage{}

Every gift carries a Frost Mark (weight timer); every oath sworn is carved in ice that never fully melts. Power requires gambling memory (Adar's ravens), accepting storm-marks (Rorg's attention), or submitting to Temple re-education (losing shrine-devotion).

minipage}

**Geography as Constraint**

[][l]{%
minipage{}

Fjords freeze in winter (longships beached, travel impossible); skerries break the tide (navigation requires local pilots); Mistlands and Valewood edges have no need of ships or harbors to claim their due. The Aberderrin Current splits flotillas; contrary swells make steering lie.

minipage}

**The Ninth Taboo manifestation**

[][l]{%
minipage{}

In any longhouse, the ninth horn blown at a feast summons the Hollow. The wise stop at eight. Those who blow the ninth see a pale figure (Adar) standing at the high table — waiting to collect a weight. Bell-towers ring eight notes; the ninth is discovered, and discovery is fatal.

minipage}

**Current Weaknesses (honest self-assessment)**

- Temple crusade needs mechanical teeth beyond “-1 die” — add Conversion [6] timer and Synthesis Tokens for blending faiths.
- Rorg/Xhak'thul syncretism needs clearer Patron mechanics — is he Storm Father (Oath of Flame) or Khemesh (Abyss)?
- Frost Mark timer needs clearer clearance conditions per season.

### Theme & Atmosphere

>
**High Jarl (Elite):**
“The sea keeps better counsel than any scribe, and the storm remembers every oath sworn upon its winds. But the frost — the frost is the witness. It preserves what the tide would wash away. A promise sworn in winter is owed until the ice melts. And the ice never truly melts.”

>
**Net-Wife (Commoner):**
“The water speaks to those who know how to listen — the way it moves tells you if the fish are running, if the weather's turning, or if something's coming that wasn't invited to the feast. My grandmother taught me to read the frost on the oar-blades. That's how I know who will live through the winter and who will feed the seals.”

**Genre / Mood:** Norse coastal saga, oath-driven honor, horror of the unwitnessed death, the tyranny of seasons, the weight of wyrd.

**Starting Location:** A longship house lined with storm-charms and whale-bone runes, salt wind clawing at the doors. A Net-Wife binds a storm-token into a PC's palm. “The Whale-Road sings,” she says. “But the Mistlands whistle back. Bring us three keel-lengths of ironwood from the Valewood edge, or the tide will take our boats in the spring. The frost remembers the shelter you took last winter. Pay, or the ice will hold it against you.”

North of the Aberderrin Sea, where fjords split the coast and skerries break the tide, dwell the Linn. They are traders and raiders in equal breath, their longships crowding the whale-road and river mouths. They descend the Ylolka like an axe-blade and cut into southern shores, or slip through the Thin Strip where the Valewood dares not touch salt. Yet even these storm-oath people dread the Mistlands and the Valewood, whose fog and trees have no need of ships or harbors to claim their due.

The Linn measure their lives in seasons, not years. There is a season for raiding (summer, when the seas are open), a season for planting (spring, when the frost breaks), a season for governance (autumn, when the ships are beached and the Thing meets), and a season for survival (winter, when the frost sets its mark). In winter, the fjords freeze, the longships are dragged into sheds, and the people gather around the longhall fires to settle debts, tell sagas, and wait for the sun to return. The winter debt is not a book — it is a set of carved oath-sticks, each notch a promise kept or broken, each knot a story still unfolding. When a Linn says a debt is “written in frost,” they mean it is unchangeable until the ice melts. And the ice, in the high north, never truly melts.

The gods of the Linn are not distant. **Adar**, the All-Father, walks the ridges in a gray cloak, his one eye watching for those who break oaths. He is a manifestation of the Oath of Flame and Light, but the Linn know him as the god of wisdom, death, and binding promises. **Rorg**, the Storm Father, rides the clouds, his hammer cracking the sky. He is a syncretic version of Xhak'thul (in the vein of Thor) — the patron of raiders and sailors, a thunder-god who laughs in the teeth of the gale. His cult is loud, proud, and dangerous — a Rorg devotee will swear a storm-oath by drinking seawater and shouting at the lightning. The Temple of Light calls him a demon. The Linn call him captain.

**What you notice first:** The smell of tar and salt fish. The creak of oars from unseen boats. The way everyone — jarl to thrall — touches a knotted cord before speaking of the sea. The oath-sticks hanging from every belt, each mark a weight carried.

**The one rule that kills newcomers:** Never name a drowned person aloud while underway. The sea collects names, and if it hears you speaking one it doesn't recognize, it may reach up to correct the debt. Also, never refuse a cup of winter mead — it is a test of your honor and your weight.

### Regional Tables

#### Spades — Places

- **Kelp-Skerry Gut** — Narrow channel where oars scrape weed and rock.
*Kelp strands like dead men's hair; row silently or the reef listens.* [TRAVEL] [STEALTH]
- **Tide-Shed** — Longship houses; tar smoke and gulls for sentries.
*Each shed holds a keel's ghost; old crews sleep under the floor planks.* [REPUTATION]
- **Wave-Gate Reef** — Just off a raiding beach; only locals know the cut.
*One wrong turn and the wave breaks over you — twice.* [TRAVEL] [DEATH]
- **Runestone Causey** — Across tidal flat; names half lost to barnacle.
*Touch the stone with your left hand. If it's warm, the ancestors approve.* [LEGEND]
- **Herring-Stairs** — Drying racks above cliff path; knives flicker like fish.
*Workers sing a counting song — eight verses, never nine.* [LABOR]
- **Winter Hall** — Turf walls, smoke-eye roof, benches crowded with shields.
*The fire never goes out. Feed it a story each night or it goes hungry.* [COMMUNITY]
- **Mistlands Maze** — Reed-channels braid and vanish; navigation by instinct.
*The reeds whisper names you've forgotten. Do not answer.* [DEATH] [FEAR]
- **Boomed Harbor** — Iron rings in whale-bone posts; controlled access.
*The chain was forged from a broken oath. It rattles when liars approach.* [AUTHORITY]
- **Aberderrin Headland** — Current rips past wreck timbers in the kelp.
*On foggy nights, the drowned signal with lanterns. Never follow.* [DEATH]
**J**: **Dolmis Waystation** — Low isle with fresh water and old weights.
*The well is lined with copper. A single dropped coin returns as a blessing.* [TRAVEL]
**Q**: **Thing-Holm** — Flat islet ringed with stones for speaking and swearing.
*The stones have ears; oaths spoken here echo for three tides. The winter oaths are kept here, frozen in a block of ice that never melts.* [JUSTICE]
**K**: **High Jarl's Seat** — Above fjord, beacon tower glaring out to sea.
*The beacon oil is mixed with whale fat. It burns green when a storm is close, blue when the winter debts are called.* [WEATHER]
**A**: **Whale-Road Horizon** — Open water where storms are born and names are made.
*Here, the sky meets the sea. Here, the dead meet the living.* [LEGEND]

#### Hearts — People & Factions

- **Net-Wife** — Reads sea like memory, sky like mood; weather-witch in all but name.
*She ties a knot for every storm she's survived. Her belt has thirty. She is the keeper of the village oath-sticks.* [COMMUNITY]
- **Steersman** — Tiller-hand never shakes, even when keel does.
*His left ear is scarred — he listened too long to a siren's promise. His oath-stick is notched for every life he's lost.* [REPUTATION]
- **Shipwright** — Pitch on palms, schedule in teeth; knows every plank's story.
*He names each timber after a dead relative. The keel is his grandmother. The ship's burden is carved into the mast.* [CRAFT]
- **Oar-Master** — Sets beat that decides if home is today or never.
*He drums on a hollowed skull. The rhythm is a prayer to Rorg. The oar-crew's debt is marked on his own arm — notches in the bone.* [SOCIAL]
- **Mist-Pilot** — Ghosts boats through marsh lanes; reed-runner with secret paths.
*He never blinks in fog. Some say he traded his blink for safe passage. His memory-cord is knotted, not notched — the knots are spells.* [STEALTH]
- **Skald** — Verses buy silence, start fights, end them; law in rhyme.
*Her tongue is forked — she can praise and curse in the same breath. She is the only one who can reshape a frost-bound oath — by composing a new verse that changes the meaning of a mark.* [JUSTICE] [SOCIAL]
- **Shield-Band** — Cousins fine with coin, better with cattle.
*They sharpen their swords on runestones. The sparks tell fortunes. Their oath-stick is shared — each mark is a blood debt owed to the band.* [COMBAT]
- **Foster-Son** — Southern coast birth; speaks both laws and subtext.
*He wears two brooches — one iron, one bone. Neither is his true allegiance. He carries two oath-sticks — one for the Linn, one for the lowlands.* [POLITICS]
- **Thing-Speaker** — Makes war into lawsuit, lawsuit into lunch.
*He carries a water-timer that runs on meltwater. When it runs out, so does your patience. He interprets the winter debts for those who cannot read ice.* [JUSTICE]
**J**: **Sea-Queen's Hand** — Envoy with seal-bag and sword-belt; queen's will made manifest.
*He never draws his blade. The threat is enough. His oath-stick is branded with the queen's mark — a seal that cannot be forged.* [AUTHORITY]
**Q**: **Sea-Queen** — Crown of hammered silver, eyes for weather and law.
*She lost an eye to a storm — or to a spy. She won't say which. She is the only one who can order the winter debts spoken.* [AUTHORITY]
**K**: **High Jarl** — First among raids, last to boast; paramount over strands.
*His beard is braided with silver from every ship he's taken. His oath-stick is a whale's rib — too long for anyone else to carry.* [REPUTATION]
**A**: **Volva of Mist** — Oath-reader whose nod stills surf; seer of tides and truth.
*She speaks once a year. The rest of the time, she listens to the fog. She reads the frost-bound oaths by touch — her fingers are scarred from counting.* [LEGEND]

#### Clubs — Complications/Threats

- **Black Squall** — Drops from clear band; oars or prayers — pick one. [WEATHER]
*The wind screams a name. Listen carefully — it might be yours. Rorg is testing your courage.*
- **Fogfall** — Sound travels, sight does not; friend and reef trade places. [WEATHER] [FEAR]
*You hear oars. Then you don't. Then they're behind you. The drowned are rowing.*
- **Boom Lift** — Harbor chain rises; schedules drown in harbor mouth. [AUTHORITY]
*The chain's links are inscribed with names of those who carry weight. Each one rattles differently. Your name is on one.*
- **Levy Clash** — Viterra's wardens arrive with polite spears. [POLITICS] [COMBAT]
*They carry a writ stamped with the queen's seal. The seal is still wet. The winter ice says the queen is owed three ships.*
- **Keel-Rot Rumor** — Crews beach mid-voyage; trust in timber fails. [DISASTER]
*The rot smells sweet — too sweet. Someone poisoned the tar. The ship's mark is missing.*
- **Feud Token** — Raid becomes wedding or funeral; oath-debt called due. [SOCIAL] [DEBT]
*A bronze ring arrives on an arrow. The meaning is clear. The ice shows the mark.*
- **Oath Matured** — Verse sworn last winter comes due today. [SOCIAL] [DEBT]
*The skald clears her throat. The room goes cold. The ice in the Thing-Holm cracks.*
- **Mistlands Miscount** — Channels “move,” cargo vanishes without witnesses. [DEATH]
*The fog lifts to reveal a different shore. Your charts are now lies. The cargo's mark is blank — someone erased it.*
- **Aberderrin Race** — Contrary currents split flotilla; half late, half lost. [WEATHER]
*The water churns like a dying man. Something beneath is feeding. The sea remembers a new debt.*
**J**: **Southron Fire-Pots** — Night-run turns to daylight; surprise ashore. [COMBAT]
*Pots shatter on the deck. The fire burns blue — alchemical. Rorg laughs. The raid's memory is now fire-scarred.*
**Q**: **Thing Injunction** — No sailing till grievance heard (hours? days?). [JUSTICE]
*The Thing-Speaker smiles. He has all the time in the world. The winter oath is frozen — no one can leave until it thaws.*
**K**: **General Muster** — Horns on every headland; all bays become spears. [AUTHORITY] [COMBAT]
*The war fleet assembles. Your ship is the smallest. Adar is watching. He counts the oaths.*
**A**: **Ground-Sea** — Long, blind swell rolls under; steering lies. [WEATHER] [DEATH]
*The swell has a rhythm — two short, one long. A signal from below. The drowned are voting.*

#### Diamonds — Rewards/Leverage

- **Harbor-Mark** — Dock without levy in named strand (once). [TRAVEL]
*The mark is a notch cut in a bone. Match it to the harbor post. The notch must be cut by the harbor master's own knife.*
- **Oar-Share** — Claim two benches on a fast longship for a season. [TRAVEL]
*The oars are carved with your name. Row well, or they'll be recarved. The oar itself is the promise.*
- **Pilot's Token** — Mist-runner guides through reed-maze safely. [TRAVEL]
*The token is a dried eel skin. Keep it dry. The pilot's memory-cord is knotted in the same pattern.*
- **Wharf-Right** — Dolmis waystation loading priority; first ashore. [TRAVEL]
*The harbormaster frowns but steps aside. Your name is now on a list.*
- **Salvage Claim** — Flotsam on reef stretch becomes “inventory.” [TRADE]
*You must name each piece before touching it. The wrong word forfeits the claim. The promise of the salvage is bound to the tide line.*
- **Thing Ruling** — Verdict in your favor that travels with you. [JUSTICE]
*The verdict is carved on a whale-rib. Carry it as a shield. The winter ice will not speak for the same dispute twice.*
- **Raid-Truce** — Immunity in named bay for one market day. [TRAVEL] [SOCIAL]
*A white banner on your mast. No one will attack — openly. The promise of the truce is the banner rope. Cut it, and the truce ends.*
- **Foster-Bond** — Guest-kin by jarl's house; hospitality guaranteed. [SOCIAL]
*You share a cup with the jarl. The cup is silver. The promise is iron. The winter ice bears a new mark — for both of you.*
- **Herring Allotment** — Priority barrels when the run hits; silver in season. [TRADE]
*The barrels are sealed with your mark. Break one to test quality. The promise of the allotment is the barrel hoop.*
**J**: **Escort Writ** — Eight shields and wolf-banner from cape to cape. [TRAVEL] [COMBAT]
*The shields are painted with a wolf's head. They die before you do. Their oath is their swords — notched for every oath kept.*
**Q**: **Queen's Audience** — Whisper exits as policy; sea-law bends. [AUTHORITY]
*The Queen's hand writes your words on vellum. The ink is her blood. The winter ice will record the audience — but not the words.*
**K**: **High Jarl's Pennon** — Levies open booms and mouths when it flies. [AUTHORITY]
*The pennon is torn from a captured ship. Fly it proudly — or else. The promise of the pennon is the ship's mast.*
**A**: **Storm-Oath Clause** — Temporary exception to any sea-law, sealed. [AUTHORITY] [MAGIC]
*The clause is whispered, never written. The sea hears and obeys — once. Rorg will remember. The winter ice will not record it — the ice cannot hold a whisper.*

### Patronage & Power

Among the Linn, power flows through oaths, kinship, and the spoken word — and through the marks carved in ice. Jarls maintain authority through successful raids and wise judgments, while skalds wield influence through their ability to immortalize deeds in verse — or damn names through satire. The Sea-Queen holds sway over the coastlands, but her rule depends on the respect of the High Jarl and the Thing-speakers who interpret ancient laws. And beneath all of them lies the frost-bound memory — the carved word, not the written one.

**For the GM:**
Power in Linn society is fluid and performance-based. Patronage often takes the form of foster-bonds, oar-shares, or raid-truces — each binding the recipient to service and reputation. To emphasize this:

- Tie rewards to visible symbols (tokens, banners, verses) that can be challenged, stolen, or voided.
- Let rival jarls issue conflicting claims, forcing players to choose whose favor matters more.
- Use the Thing-Holm and harbor gatherings as arenas for social contests, where oaths are sworn and broken.
- Introduce the Frost Mark as a recurring pressure. Every gift from a Linn comes with a weight. Players who ignore their marks may find themselves summoned to the Thing in winter.
- Let the seasons change. A winter scene should feel different from a summer raid. Use the Season's Turn to reinforce the cyclical nature of Linn life.

In Linn society, your word is your bond, and your reputation is your greatest treasure. But the frost-bound memory is patient. It waits for spring.

### Temple Crusade Mini-Generators

#### Temple Pressure Events (d6)

Roll when the Northern Crusade advances or when the GM needs a story beat.

- **Grain Fleet Arrives.** Temple ships unload cheap southern grain. Prices drop, but the old shrine offerings are forgotten. *Effect:* $+1$ tick on **Temple Pressure** timer; $+1$d on social rolls with hungry villagers for one scene.
- **Synod Court Opens.** A Thepyrgosi judge hears the first case. Feuds may be settled with penance instead of blood-silver. *Effect:* Shrine-devout characters suffer $-1$ Position in this settlement until they prove their loyalty.
- **Bell Tower Consecrated.** A bronze bell rings nine times at dawn. The old shrine bells fall silent. *Effect:* Temple-leaning characters gain $+1$d on faith actions; every midnight, the GM may spend 1 SB to have the ninth bell attract a hungry ghost.
- **Schoolmaster Arrives.** Children learn to write Temple script. Old oral traditions are called “superstition.” *Effect:* The next generation will have $+1$ Temple Devotion; players may attempt a **Synthesis Scene** to save one shrine teaching.
- **Bishop's Progress.** A high-ranking cleric tours the coast, consecrating altars. Refusal to host him marks you as an enemy of the Light. *Effect:* Begin a **Bishop's Favor** [4] timer; if it fills, the bishop demands a public oath of loyalty.
- **Iconoclasm.** Zealots burn a seastack shrine or break a Thing's oath-ring. The old patrons are furious. *Effect:* Shrine-devout characters gain a free **Vengeance Oath** String; weather and tide hazards become one step worse for 1d4 days.

#### Linn Reactions to the Temple (d12)

How a community (or a crew) responds to the crusade's advance.

- **Desperate Acceptance.** “We ate their grain. We owe them.” *Tag:* Grateful–Sullen.
- **Silent Resistance.** Shrine offerings are left in secret; Temple priests are given cold hearths. *Tag:* Ice–Hospitality.
- **Open Feud.** A clan declares the Temple an enemy. Raids on granaries begin. *Clock:* **Feud with Temple** [6].
- **Syncretic Curiosity.** Elders ask the priest to bless a shrine. “Both fires warm the hall.” *Opportunity:* Earn a **Synthesis Token**.
- **Pragmatic Split.** The jarl converts; half the thing follows, half walks out. *Clock:* **Thing Schism** [6].
- **Conversion as Revenge.** A family spurned by the old patrons embraces the Temple to spite them. *Tag:* Bitter–Righteous.
- **Bread & Bells.** The village accepts the Temple but keeps a hidden shrine to Hv\'{}tabj\"{o}rn. *Tag:* Double–Altar.
- **Heretic Burnings.** Temple zealots execute a shrine-keeper. The hall is now **Contested Ground**.
- **The Bishop's Bastard.** A priest's secret child is now a Linn raider. *String:* Blood–Secret.
- **Wave-Father's Answer.** A storm wrecks a Temple grain ship. Shrine-devout see a sign. *Effect:* $+2$ on a shrine-related roll this session.
- **Oath-Ring Saved.** A Temple judge rules that the old oath-ring is still lawful – a rare bridge-builder. *Reward:* **Ambassador Status** (one scene of neutral faith ground).
- **The Silent Bell.** The new tower's bell cracks on the ninth toll. No one can explain it. *Omen:* GM gains 2 SB for fog- or ghost-related twists.

#### Temple Missions (d6)

Quests the Temple of Light might offer to a mixed or Temple-leaning crew.

- **Recover a Stolen Relic.** A shrine-devout crew has taken a fragment of the True Candle. Find it – by negotiation or force.
- **Escort the Bishop.** Take a southern prelate through a contested fjord. Protect him from “pagan” ambushes – or arrange one.
- **Convert a Hall.** A jarl sits on the fence. Persuade him (or his skald) that the Light is good for trade. *Clock:* **Conversion** [6].
- **Burn the Shrine.** A remote seastack shrine is a navigation hazard and a gathering point for resisters. The Temple offers silver for its destruction.
- **Rescue a Synod Judge.** He was taken hostage after a biased ruling. Infiltrate the clan's winter hall and bring him out alive.
- **Forgive a Blood-Debt.** The Temple wants to end a feud by paying blood-silver from its own coffers. You must convince both sides to accept – a delicate parley.

#### Faith Tension Scenes (d6)

Quick scene starters for religious conflict.

- **The Thinglet at the Hearth.** Shrine-devout and Temple-leaning families argue over a broken betrothal. *Position:* Controlled $$ Desperate if you take sides openly.
- **Midnight at the Bell Tower.** Someone has silenced the ninth bell – by stuffing it with wool from a white bear's pelt. *Complication:* Spiritual Conflict Condition begins.
- **The Convert's Shame.** A Temple-leaning Linn begs you to smuggle her family heirloom (a shrine totem) out of the village before the bishop's agents find it.
- **Storm over the Synod Court.** V\'{e}lki answers a shrine-devout's prayer with a lightning strike on the Temple granary. *GM:* Spend 2 SB to have a priest accuse the party of witchcraft.
- **The Wandering Skald.** A singer arrives with a verse that claims the crew has a secret shrine oath. The verse is false – but now everyone believes it.
- **Dual Oath at Dusk.** A dying warrior asks to swear by both Hr{}vkn and the Light. The shrine-keeper and the Temple priest each demand you witness only their rite. *Reward:* A **Synthesis Token** if you honor both.

#### Syncretic Outcomes (d6)

When players successfully blend shrine and Temple practices, roll (or choose) a lasting effect.

- **The Shared Cairn.** A new shrine uses a Temple candle to light the old oath-ring. *Effect:* This site is now **Mixed Quarter** permanently; once per session, any character may reroll a failed faith-related roll here.
- **Witness of Both.** The crew is known as bridge-builders. *Effect:* Gain **Ambassador Status** (convert a faith-based Position penalty into a bonus once per session).
- **The Ninth Bell Silent.** The village agrees to ring only eight bells, leaving the ninth for the old patrons. *Effect:* Shrine-devout characters no longer suffer $-1$ Position in this village.
- **The Skald's Compromise.** A Temple hymn is set to an old shrine tune. *Effect:* Any Audience tag that includes “Suspicious” downgrades to “Curious” in this region.
- **Blood-Silver to the Poor.** A feud is settled by paying wergild to the Temple's poor fund – but the shrine witnesses the payment. *Effect:* The settlement counts as both a **Thing Verdict** and a **Synod Absolution**. The GM may not use this feud as a complication again.
- **The Unbroken Spiral.** A new rite is born: a white candle and a raven's feather are offered together. *Effect:* The crew gains a permanent **Synthesis Token** that refreshes every season (instead of being one-use).

### Local Patrons (Syncretic Names)

- **Adar the All-Father** — Oath of Flame and Light. *The one-eyed god of wisdom, death, and binding oaths. He watches from the ridges. His oath-stick is the frost-bound memory itself.*
- **Rorg the Storm Father** — Syncretic Xhak'thul (Thor-like). *The god of thunder, raiding, and the wild sea. His devotees swear storm-oaths by drinking seawater. He laughs at lightning. The Temple calls him a demon; the Linn call him captain.*
- **The Salted Anchor** — The Sealed Gate. *The harbor that never closes, the oath that never rusts.*
- **The Wave Mother** — Ra\'{e}yn. *The tide that carries and the storm that answers.*
- **The Drowned Chorus** — Khemesh. *The pressure beneath the keel, the weight the sea collects.*
- **The Unwritten Verse** — The Witness. *The memory that survives the drowning.*

### Lore Echoes (Cross-Expansion Hooks)

- **The Draugr Jarl (Unfinished Business):** The Thing-Holm is haunted by a jarl who died before his oath was fulfilled. He rises when a storm-oath is broken, demanding a blood-price paid in stories. The Temple of Light has sent three missionaries to lay him to rest; all three drowned in calm water. His oath-stick is frozen into the ice of the Thing-Holm. If it ever thaws, he will walk again.
- **Adar's Ravens (The Witness):** Adar is said to have two ravens, Memory and Thought, who fly across the world each day and return to whisper in his ear. A Linn skald who prays to Adar may ask one question about a forgotten weight; the GM must answer truthfully, though cryptically. The price is a memory — the skald forgets something unimportant, but it may become important later.
- **Rorg's Hammer (The Xhak'thul):** The Storm Father's hammer is said to be lodged in a cliff on the highest skerry. A character who touches the hammer and survives the lightning may invoke Rorg's wrath once per session: all enemies within Near must test Resolve (DV 4) or be Stunned for one exchange. The cost is that the character is marked by the storm — they will be struck by lightning at the worst possible moment (GM's discretion).
- **The Tide-Washed Covenant (The Hospice of the Salted Anchor):** A gray-robed healer runs a hospice on the edge of the Mistlands, treating wounded raiders and fog-mad sailors alike. She asks no payment, but she writes every name in a book that never dries. Linn captains leave offerings of fresh water before a voyage; those who refuse find their ship plagued by the drowned. The book is said to be a copy of the frost-bound oaths — but written in salt water, not ice.
- **The Ninth:** In any longhouse, the ninth horn blown at a feast summons the Hollow. The wise stop at eight. Those who blow the ninth are said to see a pale figure standing at the high table — waiting to collect a weight. The figure is Adar, checking his oath-stick.

### Linn Superstitions (burn for +1 die once)

- **Bread to the Wake:** Toss a crust over the gunwale before a voyage. Ignore the first *Black Squall* penalty. [SUPERSTITION]
- **Knot the Oar:** Tie a single knot in your oar's leather grip. Cancel *Keel-Rot Rumor* or take $-1$ die on your next rowing check (your choice). [SUPERSTITION]
- **Name to the Deep:** Whisper a dead enemy's name into the tide. Gain +1 Effect against his kin for the scene, but mark *Obligation* to the Sea-Queen. [SUPERSTITION]
- **Drink to the Storm:** Pour a cup of mead into the sea before a raid. Rorg will grant you favorable winds — but he will also expect a share of the plunder. [SUPERSTITION]

### Quick Use Notes

- Draw until you have all four suits: Spade = place, Heart = actor, Club = pressure, Diamond = leverage. Highest rank sets the main Timer (2–5 $$ 4, 6–10 $$ 6, J/Q/K $$ 8, A $$ 10).
- Diamonds are codified outcomes (rights/tokens/escorts) that change position rather than call for a roll.
- If any A appears, echo **sea-omens** — horns on wind, white horses on swell, verse unfinished until landfall, the ice cracking with memory.
